reviews.text: 游戏很错，质量也很高，画风很有特色，玩法也比较新奇。 但缺点也比较明显： 1.新手教程太简单，很多重要的东西没有说清楚，比如升级的机制，怪物的不同攻击手段。 2.如果你加上更炫酷的打击音效和特效就更好了，现在有些清汤寡水的，不够刺激。 3.没有鼠标悬浮提示，重要的UI和怪物的特质要是能加上悬浮提示就更好了，不清楚怪物的技能和各种奇遇的效果全都要靠猜。比如陷阵之志那样的。 4.肉鸽属性有点太少了，本来技能就少，升级技能又很难获得，一整把游戏下来，四个技能都拿不满升级，更别说二段升级了，希望以后可以增加技能和升级的机会。 5.难度曲线太陡了，从三章开始难度直线上升，角色的成长完全跟不上怪物的成长。随便打一下就是上百的伤害，这个时候基本只生了两级，生了三四级技能，输出根本不够看。尤其是三章的指挥官攻击欲望跟疯狗一样，基本只能在逃跑和挨打二选一，耗着耗着就把自己耗死了。 总的来说是一款质量中上的游戏，能再优化一下就更好了，我觉得最迫切的是增加肉鸽属性和更亮眼的打击音效特效，个人愚见
内容太少了，只有7关，刚好卡着我三小时通关。打完之后就只能靠加难度buff换组合来重复游玩，未免有些无聊。此外游戏日记本信息太简略了，很多技能得在对局中才能看到详情。也没有怪物图鉴

游戏想法是不错的，可惜平衡做的一坨。 虽然技能和角色自由搭配，但是只有特定一些组合才有强度，其他一些搭配连通关都是困难。 大致地形就那么几种，对玩家限制非常大，但怪物基本都是会召唤+AOE的神仙，高难度还要加上诅咒折磨。 道具数量屈指可数，大部分都是蚊子腿增益。而怪物的成长和诅咒的成长却是指数翻倍的。 我已经通关难度3，但这些局下来我觉得游戏存在着非常严重的平衡问题。如果不加以改进和优化玩家的体验，终将成为一款食之无味弃之可惜的遗憾作品。

Second to last level, bosses spawn enough bile to cover 100% of the field. Unavoidable 800 damage every 3 turns. Rest of the game is a lot of fun. If that ends my run again I'm changing my review to a negative.

Fun concept but not very well made for the listed price. There are a lot of inconsistencies but the worst part is that the bouncing predictor is often incorrect. And seeing as it is very core to the main gameplay, thats no good... It plays like a playtest, not like a 15 buck finished game, as it's not very balanced and feels unfinished. For example, the game hints that it's good to be nice to the rocks and "the will remember this" if you steal from them. But then there are no consequenses for stealing from them and you just get other equally good things for being nice to them. [spoiler] And once you meet the creator he still just gives you a curse for a boon, same as he would otherwise [/spoiler]. For now, not worth your money. If they continue working on it, it's probably going to be great, Save your cash for now unless its on heavy sale, and come back in a while.

[h3]肉鸽+弹球这种新奇的玩法，搭配可爱搞怪的卡通画风，只一眼，我就沦陷了。最终的结果可想而知——好奇心被勾起，毫不犹豫入坑了！[/h3] 当前已全成就达成，以下评测带有个人主观意识居多，如有理解不到位或错误的地方，也欢迎大佬们交流与指正（已开放评论区）。 [b]游戏当前一共有5名可选择角色，每个角色都有一个主动技能（弹射后发动）和被动技能（部分需解锁）。主动技能相当于天赋技能，不可更换，被动技能可在角色选择界面进行预览与更换。通过游戏中的事件，可赋予技能各种不同的触发或增益效果，部分效果有时候可以直接改变角色的攻击方式或当局的游戏玩法。[/b] [b]开局可两两搭配选择出场角色，下面简单说说个人对这些角色的理解：[/b] 1.侠客（初始角色） 主要攻击方式为撞击，中规中矩，直来直去，主动技能在增加弹射力后，虽然可撞击的单位增加了，但是经过多次弹射后的落点变得较为不可控，风险与收益不对等。也许后续开发出玩法与技能构筑会变得强力。 2.斧哥（开局加入） 当前T0级别的角色，主动技能在弹射后，以自身为中心进行AOE攻击，不管是搭配护盾吸收增加生存能力，还是搭配攻击后会触发某些特殊效果增加伤害能力，甚至连锁效果，斧哥都是你通关路上最有利的帮手。记得优先提升主动技能的攻击范围。 3.蛙女（难度1加入） 这个角色的优点很明显（输出上限非常高），缺点也同样突出（启动异常慢）。主要表现在收集一定数量的青蛙后，搭配赋予的多段攻击和异常效果，可以非常轻松秒掉高血量的敌方单位，但是前提是需要你尽可能多的收集场地上的青蛙。如果同时锁定多个敌方单位，总输出将被分摊，且输出目标变得随机，无法进行准确击杀。偶尔未收集的青蛙会跟敌方单位重叠或刷新在非常危险的区域，导致我方需要好几个回合进行收集——如果换成其他强力角色，可能已经完成当前关卡了......该角色同样需要优先提升主动技能的锁定范围，在低难度敌方单位较少的地图表现尚可，高难度未知。 4.枪手（难度2加入） 未赋予技能效果时，只能通过撞击进行锁定输出，攻击方式为可穿透敌方单位但无法穿透地形的直线攻击。当增加主动技能射击次数和子弹反弹效果后，往往能打出很多意料之外又让人眼前一亮的效果。 5.火箭女（难度3加入） 主动弹射后，靠撞墙或者撞击敌方单位来发射火箭，需要精确计算停留点周围有没有用敌方单位： 有敌方单位：火箭直接在敌方单位所在位置爆炸，发射次数与撞击次数相关，且爆炸范围内，自身也会受到一定的伤害。 无敌方单位：火箭直接在自身所在位置爆炸（自爆），发射次数与撞击次数相关。 虽然伤害非常可观，但是在复杂地形处或者敌方单位较多时，需要对敌方单位进行精准打击却不使自身受到伤害却非常困难。可能跟我刚解锁并且还没熟悉这个角色的操作有关吧，使用前请三思！ （介绍完所有角色，相信各位心中一定有了自己认为最合适的开局组合，其实通关不难，除了运气之外，唯手熟尔！） [b]关于宝物的选择：[/b] 当前的宝物种类不多，部分宝物需要通过达成游戏内置成就进行解锁。首先，复活甲的优先级永远最高，前期可以选择增加经验或者增加废品获得的宝物，之后以伤害加成相关的宝物优先，其次选择护盾相关的宝物。宝物并非“唯一”，且数量可叠加，特别是通过“发明家事件”将不同名的宝物转换成某件同名宝物后，将会出现由量变引发质变的效果。 [b]关于敌方单位：[/b] 金色底座：本场战斗的敌方首领，后期会出现多个首领单位，全部击杀后即可立即结束战斗。 普通底座：普通单位，可选择性击杀，一般优先击杀挡路的，或者攻击方式比较恶心的。 铁制底座：无法被破坏的单位，部分单位即使被打败，依旧会重生。 [b]关于诅咒：[/b] 高难度的诅咒随处可见，特别是血量低时，给予的选择更少，哪怕使用SL大法，随机次数也有限——任何事件都可以通过SL大法进行1~2次的随机尝试，一般3次过后，选项还是没有改变就基本可以确定下来了（金币随机功能需要通过局外解锁获得）。 （部分诅咒的负面效果实在太强力，拿的诅咒数量一多，体验基本全无，可以找到“智猴事件”，以付出一定的血量为代价，选择性清除负面影响最大的诅咒。） [b]关于对当前游戏存在问题的建议：[/b] 1.当前地图太少，翻来翻去就是那几张图，且地图太小，加上高难度堆怪严重，陷阱地形恶心，生存空间更是被大大压缩，很多怪又都是AOE伤害，想要全身而退无异于痴人说梦，容错率极低，希望尽快进行优化。 2.部分诅咒效果过分强力，选择时根本不会考虑（狗都不选），需要进行一系列的平衡。 3.增加敌方单位行动的伤害预览以及行动顺序，以便于玩家计算自身的伤害承受范围（很多时候，我都可以承受几次攻击，但是被多次攻击强制位移后，又被对面好几个单位的一套combo带走是真的会谢）。 4.通过部分诅咒效果，还有部分宝物效果不难看出，开发者是提倡我们在战斗中进行角色轮换攻击的。但是实际上，“铁匠事件”在技能赋予时，给予的效果太多太杂，想要选到合适的效果太难——往往通关时，部分角色的技能都还有几个框是空的，这就导致我更习惯使用技能成型的角色而不会刻意为了触发角色切换效果去使用另一名角色。 要么增加切换角色带来的羁绊效果，要么在诅咒效果上做一些改动，或者将“铁匠事件”中的赋予选择改成[u]每个角色都可选择一次[/u]，力求平衡两名角色的能力，不然换成任何玩家都会优先选择成型后的角色。 5.之前增加了角度微调，力度微调也赶紧加上来啊！！！每个回合基本就是在瞄准这个环节耗费了大量的时间！请百万火急加紧优化！ （暂时就想到这些，欢迎各位进行补充！） 完美的角度和刚刚好的力度，加上那么一点点运气，相信这些因素是每个游玩这款游戏的玩家都希望拥有的。不过这款游戏嘛，对游戏机制的理解也是挺重要的！ 当前游戏作为新发，还有太多需要改进的地方，我们不妨让这颗“弹球”再滚一会！ [code] 点击关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/26214428] 電玩狂熱愛好者 [/url] [h1]我在肉鸽游戏里打桌球[/h1] 玩过肉鸽游戏，玩过桌球游戏，但肉鸽加台球还真是第一次玩。《肉鸽弹弹奇兵》是一款有着美系卡通画风，从海盗题材做展开，将爬塔式的推进和桌面台球碰撞相结合的创意肉鸽游戏。 游戏的局外部分其实类似于爬塔，玩家从遭受海难到成功登顶，一个完整的流程总共有七个关卡。每个关卡里就是类爬塔的分支路线推进，路线上会有战斗、篝火、升级、奇遇、商店、BOSS等的房间，一路推进打败BOSS后就能进入下一个图。 游戏的局内战斗，每一次的战斗是一个不规则的场景（理解为桌台），不同房间内的场景里会有些些许的不同，比如障碍物、陷阱等东西，玩家所操控的角色和敌人都是分布在场景上的一个个棋子（理解为球或者弹珠）。玩家需要在战斗过程中调整棋子弹射的角度、力度来攻击敌人，击杀首领或全部击杀后就能通过房间。我之所以用打桌球来形容，是因为两者共性很多。回合制的战斗，能精细调整的弹射方向和力度，而且在玩家微调时会大致的显示发射后自身棋子的位置以及碰撞后对方棋子的位置，能更好的进行策略规划，当然大力出奇迹时多次弹射位置是无法估计的。 游戏中随着流程推进玩家能使用多种角色，每个角色都有各自的特点（自带一个不可更换的初始效果，其他的效果就是肉鸽部分的内容了，比如初始的两个角色一个能多次弹射来造成伤害，一个落位后能旋转攻击造成范围伤害等等），每次的战斗只能选择两种角色来搭配使用（在回合制战斗中可以随意更换）。而敌方棋子，不同的敌人会有着不同的攻击方式、血量、技能等，同时敌人还会有着等级的区别，比如普通底座和黄金底座，黄金底座就是首领，击杀所有首领就能全灭普通敌人，稍稍增强了策略深度。游戏中角色有两种血量，一种是普通生命值，通过路线中的篝火来恢复部分，一种是护盾，护盾每次的战斗都会恢复。 游戏的肉鸽部分，包含了角色的技能、诅咒、路线上的奇遇等、商店售卖物等。技能可以很直观的增强角色的战斗能力，并且在往后的奖励往往也是同个方向持续增强。比如初始的侠客角色有一个弹射后造成燃烧效果的技能，多次弹射可以让很多目标连锁的着火，而锤哥有个落位旋转攻击后附带炸弹在之后爆炸。诅咒的负面效果也很明显就是了，诅咒一多体验很差，然后商店售卖物效果倒是很丰富（什么每次切换角色增伤啊、切换角色恢复盾牌啊、累积废弃物来获得增益BUFF啊、），而且同种物品可以多次叠加生效（比如一个叫望远镜的物品可对远距离的攻击进行增伤）。 游戏的难度其实是不低的，主要是难度曲线设计的不合理，前几关难度非常低，到了四五关就开始难了，肉鸽选择上不欧的话伤害和BOSS完全没得比，攻击范围又广，总共才1000血一个机关无视护盾的扫我300血，然后还很多小怪，躲都躲不过来。然后没有怪物图鉴，每种怪物需要玩家来记忆特点、技能等。内容也偏少，总共就七关，后续的流程就是用强加诅咒来增加游戏难度。 总结，《肉鸽弹弹奇兵》是一款玩法非常新颖的游戏，它将常规的爬塔肉鸽和桌球碰撞结合起来了，融合下的玩法很有意思，玩着很上头。但游戏目前肉鸽的内容不够丰富，难度曲线不合理，需要改进。整体感觉还是很有潜力的，值得期待一下。 [quote]关注鉴赏组：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45134494]浮生评测[/url] ←"浮生若梦，一鉴倾心，邀您共赏人间烟火" 加入Steam组：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/LLFLLFF]浮生评测[/url]←“一起追寻'浮生若梦'般的游戏体验” 开始“浮生若梦”鉴赏组的奇幻之旅！[/quote]

TL;DR: Starts like buried treasure, plays like loose change. Flick Shot Rogues makes a strong first impression. You’re a pirate slinging yourself into enemies like a cannon ball, clearing encounters, progressing across regions, and taking down bosses. At first it feels like a keeper, but soon you realise the first impression is the only one it has. With no evolving mechanics, every run ends up feeling the same. Strategising feels like guesswork, flicking is only so precise, and hits never feel especially impactful. What the game needs is a second layer: single-use abilities, smarter enemy patterns, destructible environments, etc. The core idea works, but the execution never gets past its opening act. The Highs - Original concept with plenty of potential - Easy to pick up, immediately clear mechanics The Lows - Repetitive from the start - No real strategic depth - Hits lack the visual feedback to feel satisfying - Presentation feels unfinished from map to UI If the gameplay appeals to you, you might find something similar in Drop Pockets. 🧙🏻‍♂️If this review helped, check my profile for more takes built on the same bar.

[h2]Missed Potential[/h2] You probably haven’t seen many Flick Shot style games as Flick Shot Rogues will likely be your first real encounter with a genre that hasn’t seen much innovation in recent years. Essentially, you flick units around a board, colliding with other units, enemies, and terrain while applying modifiers and effects to maximize your damage. Unfortunately, most games in this niche have been underappreciated or have faded away, either shutting down or losing their player base, that's so depressing, because it genuinely has the power to drive itself. I was excited for Flick Shot Rogues because I love this sub-genre of strategy. Swapping characters and building synergies offers so much potential, but in this case, the execution feels weak and underdeveloped. The game doesn’t capitalize on the genre’s strengths, leaving its most promising elements feeling lackluster. [h2]Issues[/h2] While you can choose between two characters, each with their own abilities and passives, the only real variation comes from the secondary abilities you assign them and play around them. For example, pairing the Froggomancer with a secondary character with the FireFly passive allows you to focus on specific upgrades, like multi-frog shot, ricochet and simply drift near (without touching) enemy units while targeting fly spawns. This strategy can rack up damage numbers in the hundreds or thousands with minimal effort. Note, the average damage you do by default is 20 and as a high of 300, without any big modifiers. The game is easily broken by ignoring the intended strategy and exploiting these mechanics. Swapping characters becomes unnecessary, and since the health pools are shared, the potential for deeper tactics, like swapping to a tankier character to absorb damage between turns, goes unrealized. This reduces the depth and challenge, leaving the gameplay feeling shallow and less engaging when all you want to do is abuse the character that's currently decked out enough to take on the enemies forces. Which is another issue. You just need to take out the golden units. Then everything else disappears. So it becomes even less of a strategy and more of a get in and get out approach. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] Overall, Flick Shot Rogues is a short experience. While modifiers exist to make subsequent runs harder, they don’t significantly change the gameplay. My biggest gripe is with the golden enemies that spam turrets from tight positions and also apply spikes that keep you from approach them every off turn. If you’re struggling with repositioning, it’s easy to get stuck or knocked away before you can even approach them, especially depending on your character choices. For a first attempt at the sub-genre, it’s decent for a single playthrough, but lacks the depth or replayability to keep players coming back. Is it a hard game? Nah, pretty simple. Might run into some annoying instances where you have to sacrifice yourself to some damage to reach an enemy, but overall easy. “A Clever Idea That Fights Against Itself” Flick Shot Rogues immediately caught my attention because it tries something genuinely different from most roguelikes out there, and I’ll always respect developers willing to experiment instead of copying trends. During my initial hours with the game, I actually enjoyed parts of the experience and could clearly see the creativity behind its design. The biggest issue for me, however, was the controls. While the flick-shot mechanic is definitely unique, it often felt more frustrating than satisfying. Too many moments felt like I was fighting the controls instead of mastering them, and simple actions occasionally became irritating due to how imprecise or awkward the movement and aiming could feel. Because of this, the pacing never fully clicked. Roguelikes usually thrive on momentum, flow, and that “one more run” feeling, but here the mechanics constantly interrupted that rhythm for me. Instead of feeling exciting and fast-paced, many encounters ended up feeling slower and more cumbersome than they should have. That said, I did enjoy the progression system. Unlocking new content and seeing gradual improvement gave me motivation to keep playing longer than I otherwise might have. The game also deserves praise for its presentation. The art direction is fantastic, the pirate-themed worldbuilding has a lot of charm, and the music fits the atmosphere extremely well. There’s clearly a strong creative vision here. Unfortunately, some of the characters felt hit-or-miss gameplay-wise, which became another issue affecting longevity. Certain characters were genuinely fun, while others made runs feel significantly less enjoyable. Over time, that inconsistency made it harder for me to stay invested. Ultimately, Flick Shot Rogues feels like a game with a fantastic foundation that just didn’t fully come together for me. I honestly think with more refined controls and smoother gameplay flow, this could have been something special. There’s a great idea here, I just don’t think the execution reaches the same level as the concept.

Flick Shot Rogues has a great hook. The idea of lining up a shot and flicking your hero across the board, chaining collisions and combos, is tactile and satisfying. There's skill in reading the board, judging angles, and shooting your disc through a crowd of crabs and monkeys to set off a chain reaction. The game is at its best when it forces you to bounce your guy into a few walls and enemies, needing you to predict the trajectories beyond the aim markers (though it feels like you should have much higher shot power to really maximize the fun in this). The cutesy pirate-themed art, the monkey island-like music, and the physics-driven puzzle of each encounter make those first few hours feel fresh and inventive. The problem is what happens after those first few hours. The run structure gets repetitive and the runs themselves aren't varied enough to make you want to keep winning them. Each attempt sends you through the same sequence of biomes and essentially the same encounters, and because so much of the game's content is locked behind a slow meta-progression, you spend a long time replaying near-identical runs just to try to gain a few Profile Levels. You're doing the same thing over and over, going crazy watching the same opening stages roll by. A good roguelite uses repetition as a way to promote variety: new builds, synergies, harder zones coupled with your better understanding of the mechanics. Here it's just a chore.

Flick Shot Rogues was genuinely such a pleasant surprise for me. I got this in a bundle, expecting it to be a great idea with a bad execution. But this game does such a great job at making the most out of it's unique concept, and it is so very [b] [i] very fun. [/i] [/b] You have 5 characters, each with two variants to unlock. The major areas of the game are always the same, but the paths within those areas have different risks and benefits to encourage you to take them. Enemy variety is a tad bit lacking, yet that doesn't diminish the replayability in fighting them. But the most important part IMO: The game never neuters your power. Some games will see a way that you can become overpowered and nerf things, or prevent combos, etc. This game doesn't do that, you can become effectively godly in terms of power and I cannot understate how fun that makes the game. Not even to mention the adorable art style, the addictive sound design, and the fact that I've only ever encountered one single bug/glitch in 25+ hours. Such a genuinely well built, well executed game. I love it and highly recommend it.

Obligatory "what a shame Steam doesnt offer a neutral view" disclaimer. "Deep as a Puddle" is a phrase I think this game suits very well, I agree with the other negative Reviews. In 1 run you will have seen every normal enemy this game has to offer. In 3 runs or so you will have seen every boss and every arena this game has to offer too. With playtime you unlock more characters, more "weapon modifiers", more "relics" and more choices you can do in your run. However with the lack of enemy or arena variety, none of these feel very unique or special. There isnt much variety for your build, even after unlocking a bit you will see the same 5 modifier choices in every run, and none of these feel cool or crazy, it makes them all blend in with each other, and none of these even will give you a "build", its more so just different skills that dont synergize with each other. There is a level up system that just as easily couldnt exist, its an arbitrary way to fake "progression" in a run. If the devs just didnt give more health or damage to enemys nothing would change, this level up system doesnt offer anything because you cant really lose enough exp. in a run for it to matter. Its useless flair. This game really is not a good Roguelite game, and if youre here for the Roguelite aspect you should skip this one. If youre here purely for the "Flick" aspect I think you will have a very fun time with this. I'd say get it on a Sale no matter what, because compared to other games in this price range I have seen way better. As a basis, if I didnt have a neurotic compulsion to 100% every achievement in games, I would have had 5 hours on this game without buyers regret and be very content with the 45% sale I got this. But trying to get anything more out of this game will make you feel frustrated. I feel like this game would have worked way better as a linear story based game instead of a Roguelite.

Play Time: 26hrs Achievements: 46 of 46 Date/Version: June 28th 2026 Rating: 7 1/2 out of 10 FlickShot Rogues: A “flicking” board game style game that's based in the digital world. You have your pirates who'll use a “slay the spire” grid like mapping system. This game does have a very tactical “feel” to it. As knowing your abilities, and the enemies is key in this game especially at higher difficulties. You'll fight against many of the same enemies, each biom has their own unique enemies. Flick your character into danger and away from danger, create unique teams to win or ultimately get yourself some treasure! (Potential Spoilers) Characters you can play: You have 5 unique characters each one comes with a variation you can play after beating Doom 5 (the difficulty) setting in the game. These characters require you to learn unique combos as in “bonus” abilities that will link with your unique characters play style. You play with two characters at the same time, and the game has the option to auto change to the other character so you don't have to manually do this. Curses: The game features curses, these curses are exactly what you think they are negative side effects during your game play. For Example you may have a curse where if you don't switch characters between turns you'll receive damage. Or at the start of the battle explosive kegs may spawn. Enemies: The enemy variety is a bit samey but each biom has it's own unique enemies and bosses. The game does a fantastic job at switching up the behavior of said enemies, and what you can do to combat said enemies. Difficulties: This is where the game does a great job leading a person into this idea it's more than just flicking and making sure you can “hit your mark”. There's a clearing curve to this game, and you need to also learn some of the enemies patterns. It isn't much but there are plenty of difficulties to choose from. I beat the game on Doom difficulty 10 and with 9 curses. I believe the game goes up to maybe doom 15 or higher. In any case you need to beat Doom 5 with each character to not only unlock variants for those characters but also to unlock the higher doom difficulty. Skills & Abilities: You chose your two starting character they have their own talents with their own talent tree. But you also get unique abilities to start off with. These can be combined to create some broken combos. And you may find combos between two characters and their talent they start with. Random Events & Music: The random events are nice, and you can control the RNG for the most part. Yes there is some RNG but it's not terrible The music wasn't terrible either nothing like a work of masterful art but hey it was enjoyable. I was initially worried about the pace of the game, playing it is a bit more fun than I thought it would be. I don't regret my purchase one bit. Fun game, must play for those looking into a physics style board game. PROS: Unique Characters Unique Enemies Fantastic Learning Curve Fantastic Difficulty settings Amazingly accurate hit boxes. Fun game that doesn't overstay it's welcome. The art was enjoyable. NEUTRAL: CONS:

A physics-based roguelike which plays as you can imagine from the promo video. Pretty decent fun and number of ways to unleash chaos on the enemies on the board, depending on how you combine the heroes (you pick 2 for each run) and their artifacts and trinkets. My impression so far is that many of these combinations are quite balanced, some characters start off more powerful than others, but as they grow through a run this can turn around. Some runs may seem difficult while others may seem walks in the park depending on the synergies you end up building along the run, as happens often in the genre, which adds to the interest. Variety of scenarios and enemies is on the short side of the spectrum, but given the different combinations of skills you can build your run around, you end up getting more variation due to the different strategies you need to follow to defeat them. On higher difficulties one bad shot can get you in a difficult situation quickly, so you also need to think plays through a bit if you don't want to end up overwhelmed. Playing on a Steam Deck, it's a good game for a handheld. All in all good fun :) .
